blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets on your Mac

Since Google Sheets runs in the browser, treat it like a native application to save time. Open Chrome and navigate to sheets.google.com. Click the three dot menu in the top right corner. Select Cast, Save, and Share. Then click Install page as app. This puts a shortcut in your Dock or Launchpad. You can now switch to this window using ⌘ + Tab just like any other Mac app.

Market research involves large datasets that often require cleaning. You likely spend hours removing duplicates or fixing formatting. Use the built in tools to save your energy for the actual analysis. If you find a column of messy text, use the Data menu to split it. If you have duplicate rows, use the Data > Data cleanup > Remove duplicates path. These steps stop you from doing manual work that eats up your day.
Using keyboard shortcuts to save time

Your hands should rarely leave the keyboard when you are deep in a spreadsheet. Press ⌘ + / to bring up the full list of shortcuts. Common ones include ⌘ + ⇧ + H for Find and Replace. Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 to hide rows and ⌘ + ⌥ + 0 to hide columns. These small movements add up to hours of saved time over a month of research work.
Common mistakes analysts make in Sheets

items: Keeping too many browser tabs open while working on heavy sheets.
Using complex formulas that break when you insert new rows.
Forgetting to check the revision history after a collaborative session.
Ignoring the cell limit when importing massive raw survey data files.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native desktop app. You should create a Progressive Web App shortcut in Chrome for a better experience.

faq.question: How do I see all shortcuts in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / on your keyboard to open the shortcut helper menu.

faq.question: What is the cell limit for a single spreadsheet?
faq.answer: As of September 2026, the limit is 20 million cells per spreadsheet.
